correctness.rationale: The positive Zak exponent leads to Fourier aliases n+omega with phases exp(2 pi i(n+omega)x), by taking Fourier coefficients of exp(-2 pi i omega x)Z. The sinc power and first derivatives are summable uniformly on compact coordinate ranges for m>=3; the parenthetical uniformity in proof step 1 should be read on bounded ranges such as the fundamental square, not as uniform convergence of fixed-index partial sums on R^2. The finding only needs the bounded ranges. On omega=1/2+s/m the n=0,-1 amplitudes are [cos(pi s/m)/(1±2s/m)]^m; their logarithms and s derivatives converge uniformly on bounded s. The remaining aliases are bounded by summable inverse odd-frequency powers, also after x or scaled-frequency differentiation. For r in [0,1/2] the tail is at most 2 a sum_{j>=1}(2j+1)^(-m), the second-to-first amplitude ratio is at most e^(-4u), and a/h_m>=e^(cu) because log(sin(pi r)/(2r))/(1/2-r) has a positive continuous extension. This gives strict exclusion outside a bounded scaled strip for fixed tau. The limit's level boundary has zero area by vertical sections; their sublevel lengths produce A(tau). Substitution t=cos(pi x) in that integral reduces the small-tau leading term to the semicircle integral on [-tau/2,tau/2] divided by pi; the relative Taylor error is O(tau^2). At the central zero, paired half-integer aliases give a negative real x derivative and negative imaginary omega derivative, with the sums in RESULT.md:81–82. Odd m gives positive-term sums and even m positive alternating sums, hence the determinant is strictly positive for every m>=3 with the stated sharp error. The known zero uniqueness also matches the centered convention. Inspected CHECKER.py, CHECKER_OUTPUT.txt and VERIFICATION.md; the reported finite diagnostics are not a proof of confinement or convergence and were not rerun.
